bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Customer concentration (Maruti Suzuki 60%); Delay in new model SOPs (Honda, Maruti MPV); Raw material price volatility (though pass-through exists); Execution risk on export ramp-up; Competition in CVJ segment (GKN, MTN).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes strict cost control and temporary nature of margin headwinds (mix, forex accounting, tariffs); Confident on capacity utilization ramp-up driving ROCE recovery; Transparent on CWIP impact on ratios.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Accounting distortion: Forex gains on import payments booked as 'Other Income' rather than reducing material cost, artificially inflating material costs by INR 62M (0.23% margin impact); CVJ is 100% localized with no imports, offering better margin potential than imported-content steering gears; CWIP of INR 411Cr is a hidden asset not yet generating revenue, masking true operational efficiency.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting ~INR 800Cr incremental revenue over next 1-2 years from capacity utilization; Margin: Expect improvement as product mix normalizes (Honda recovery) and high-margin CVJ/exports scale; Order Inflow: Brazil exports starting May '26 (70k units ramping to 500k); Capex: INR 250Cr total for Gujarat plant (INR 130Cr spent), remaining INR 100Cr+ in FY27.

outlook.body: New SOPs secured: Maruti Suzuki e-Vitara, Victoris, upcoming MPV EV (Oct '26); Honda SUV EV (Dec '26); Brazil export order (Stellantis) ramping from 70k to 500k units; CVJ capacity expanded to 7.54 lakh units (2 lines operational, 3rd coming).

outlook.body: CVJ market share target of 15% (currently supplying Grand Vitara, Hyryder, e-Vitara, Victoris); Export expansion to Brazil (Stellantis) and renewed US opportunities; Honda business recovery with new EV SUV; Potential future driveline products (driveshafts) post-CVJ stabilization.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JTEKT India delivered 11% sales growth in FY26, outpacing the 9% PV market, driven by GST cuts boosting Maruti Suzuki volumes and new SOPs (e-Vitara/Victoris), though full-year EBITDA margins dipped 10bps to 7.5% due to adverse product mix (Honda decline) and accounting forex distortions. The thesis hinges on the rapid utilization of recently commissioned CVJ and Gear lines (currently under-utilized) and the successful ramp-up of exports to Brazil and the US, which should drive ROCE recovery from current depressed levels as CWIP converts to revenue-generating assets.

risks.note: The BRSR reports manufacturing and assembling of automotive components as 99.19% of turnover with exports contributing only 2.58% of total turnover, so nearly all revenue is tied to one activity and to Indian OEM demand; revenues are largely business-to-business to OEM customers as a tier 1 supplier.
risks.risk: Single-activity concentration on the automotive OEM cycle, overwhelmingly domestic

risks.note: Identified by the Company as a material issue: manufacturing activities involve operational hazards that may lead to injuries, production disruption and legal liabilities, with negative impact stated as medical expenses, compensation cost, production loss, legal liability and reputational damage. Mitigation is a stronger safety culture, KY activities, machine safeguarding, safety patrols, behaviour-based safety, training and audits.

Flagged as a material risk that may lead to accidents, injuries and production interruptions; mitigation is interlocks, guarding improvements, emergency stop systems, residual pressure control and safety automation, which itself carries investment and maintenance cost.

Listed as a material issue — standard of work may suffer on the exit of experienced employees, high turnover disrupts workflow and decreases productivity, and there is a high cost associated with recruiting, hiring and training replacements. Permanent worker turnover was 12.28% and permanent employee turnover 6.87% in FY 2025-26, both improved from 17.50% and 8.77% in FY 2024-25. Mitigation is robust succession planning for all critical roles and structured induction.

Contractor activities may introduce safety hazards, accidents and compliance issues, with accident liabilities, project delays and reputational impact as the stated downside; mitigated through contractor induction, permit systems, supervision, competency evaluation and audits.

Fire incidents may occur due to oils, electrical systems and hot work activities, with asset damage, downtime and insurance costs as the stated impact; mitigation is emergency drills, fire detection systems, hot work permits, firefighting training and regular inspections.

Non-compliance with environmental, safety and labour regulations may result in penalties, legal actions and operational disruptions, including shutdown risk; mitigation is periodic compliance evaluations, internal audits, statutory monitoring, legal updates and training. The Board's Report separately notes the Company has a detailed Risk Management Policy that the Board periodically reviews.
